hypothesis_text: Gap depth vs M_p follows Kanagawa power law (Sigma_gap/Sigma_0 ~ K^{-1}) for M_p < 2 M_Jup
verdict_rationale: The FARGO3D simulation analysed (fargo_skill_test) was run for only ~1-2 output snapshots, capturing only the initial unperturbed condition. Gap opening requires ~100-200 orbital periods at the planet location. The setup file gap_1Mjup.par is already correctly configured for 1000 orbits (Ntot=20000, Ninterm=200); the simulation simply needs to be launched and run to completion before the Kanagawa prediction can be numerically tested.

why_118x_depletion_1MJup.summary: At 1 M_Jup / 1 M_sun with h/r=0.05 and alpha=1e-3, the Kanagawa parameter K = q^2/(h^5 * alpha) = (9.548e-4)^2 / (0.05^5 * 1e-3) = 2916, placing the planet deep in the nonlinear gap-opening regime (K/K_open = 2916/25 = 116.6). The Kanagawa formula Sigma_gap/Sigma_0 = 1/(1+0.04K) = 1/117.6 = 8.5e-3 follows from a momentum balance argument: for large K the one-sided Lindblad torque deposited by the planet exceeds the viscous restoring flux by a factor ~K, so the steady-state gap satisfies Sigma_gap/Sigma_0 ~ (0.04K)^{-1}.
why_118x_depletion_1MJup.Hill_sphere_check: R_H/H = (q/3)^{1/3} / h = (3.183e-4)^{1/3} / 0.05 = 0.0683 / 0.05 = 1.37. The Hill sphere is 37% larger than the pressure scale height, so the planet strongly excites non-linear spiral shocks rather than linear Lindblad resonances. This is the physical trigger for the deeply nonlinear gap.
why_118x_depletion_1MJup.physical_mechanism: The planet launches one-armed spiral density waves at Lindblad resonances. For K >> K_open the spiral shocks are strong enough to push gas on both sides of the orbit outward/inward faster than viscous diffusion refills the gap. The steady-state depth is set by the balance between planetary angular-momentum deposition rate and viscous diffusion flux, yielding Sigma_gap/Sigma_0 ~ K^{-1} (Kanagawa et al. 2016 eq. 4; bibcode 2016PASJ...68...43K).
why_118x_depletion_1MJup.calibration_warning: The Kanagawa formula is empirically calibrated from 2D isothermal simulations up to K ~ O(1000). At K = 2916 the formula is at the edge of its calibration range; the systematic uncertainty on the predicted depth is ~30%. 3D and non-isothermal effects add a further ~20% correction (see warnings).

why_no_gap_at_t0.summary: Snapshot 0 is the initial condition (t = 0). No angular-momentum exchange has yet occurred. The surface density is the unperturbed power-law Sigma(r) = Sigma_0 * r^{-0.5}, hence Sigma_gap/Sigma_0 = 1.0 by construction.
why_no_gap_at_t0.gap_opening_timescale: Gap opening requires the planet to complete ~100-200 orbits at its semi-major axis. For the planet at a = 20 au, one orbit = 2*pi code-time units = ~89.4 yr. Gap saturation therefore requires t_gap ~ 100-200 x 89.4 yr = 9000-18000 yr. The fargo_skill_test run captured only the initial snapshot; no physical integration time has elapsed.
why_no_gap_at_t0.code_time_context: The fargo_skill_test analysis reports n_torque_columns=10 and planet_torque_last=0.0, consistent with snapshot 0 (no integrated torque). The gap_1Mjup.par file is already configured for 1000 orbits (Ntot=20000, DT=pi/10, 1 orbit = 20 DT steps), which is sufficient for full gap saturation. The required action is simply to run this simulation.

dustpy_amax_profile.summary: The a_max(r) profile reflects two distinct size-limiting regimes. In the warm inner disc (r < ~30-50 au) the dominant relative velocity is turbulence-driven: v_turb ~ sqrt(alpha) * c_s * sqrt(St), which rises with temperature. Grains grow until v_turb equals v_frag = 10 m/s, giving a_frag ~ (2 Sigma_g) / (pi rho_s) * v_frag^2 / (alpha c_s^2). Because c_s increases inward (T ~ r^{-0.5}), a_frag decreases inward, explaining the small a_max at 10 au. In the cold outer disc (r > ~50 au), turbulent velocities are low and the size-limiting process is radial drift: grains grow until radial drift removes them before another collision, giving a_drift ~ (2 Sigma_d) / (pi rho_s) * v_K^2 / (c_s^2) * epsilon / |d ln P / d ln r|, which can be large at large r.

stated_values.regime_10au: fragmentation limited (turbulence sets relative velocity ceiling)
stated_values.regime_100au: drift limited (radial drift removes grains before fragmentation)

dustpy_amax_profile.stokes_number_estimate_10au: St(10 au) ~ pi/2 * rho_s * a_frag / Sigma_g ~ pi/2 * 1.5 * 1.95e-4 / Sigma_g(10 au) << 1, consistent with well-coupled sub-micron grains
dustpy_amax_profile.data_verification_note: CAUTION: Independent extraction from data/dust/iceline_test/data0009.hdf5 yields a_max(10 au) = 24.3 cm (all size bins populated) and a grid spanning only r = 1.1-89.7 au with Nr=20. The stated result of 1.95e-4 cm at 10 au may originate from a different DustPy run configuration or a different definition of a_max (e.g., surface-density-weighted mean vs. maximum populated bin). This discrepancy is flagged in the warnings section.

theory_comparison.Kanagawa_formula_status: The 1 M_Jup / alpha=1e-3 / h/r=0.05 parameter set gives K = 2916, which is at the high end of the Kanagawa (2016) calibration range. The predicted Sigma_gap/Sigma_0 = 8.5e-3 is a strong prediction that should be testable once the FARGO3D simulation reaches t > 100 orbits.

DSHARP_comparison.comment: 20 protoplanetary discs imaged at 1.25 mm with 35 mas resolution. Nearly all show annular sub-structure. Gap widths and depths qualitatively consistent with planets in the 0.1-1 M_Jup range under the Kanagawa formula.

DSHARP_comparison.survey: DSHARP — Huang et al. (2018), gap and ring catalogue
DSHARP_comparison.comment: Systematic catalogue of 38 gaps across the DSHARP sample. Measured dust gap depths (delta = 1 - I_min/I_0) span 0.1-0.95. A 1 M_Jup planet at 20 au in a disc with h/r=0.05 would produce a dust gap with delta ~ 0.99 (nearly complete dust depletion), broadly consistent with the deepest observed DSHARP gaps.

DSHARP_comparison.survey: DSHARP — Zhang et al. (2018), planet mass inference
DSHARP_comparison.comment: Inverted the Kanagawa formula to infer planet masses from DSHARP gap widths. For the deepest gaps, inferred planet masses are 0.5-3 M_Jup, consistent with our test case.

DSHARP_comparison.survey: Kanagawa et al. (2016), gap depth formula
DSHARP_comparison.comment: Source of Sigma_gap/Sigma_0 = 1/(1 + 0.04K). Used directly in this study.

DSHARP_comparison.survey: Kanagawa et al. (2017), gap width formula
DSHARP_comparison.comment: Provides the gap half-width Delta_gap = 0.41 (K/4)^{1/4} * a_p. For K=2916 this predicts Delta_gap / a_p ~ 0.41 * (729)^{0.25} ~ 0.41 * 5.19 ~ 2.1 H. Should be measurable once the simulation runs.

discrepancies.description: The FARGO3D run analysed (fargo_skill_test) captured only snapshot 0 (initial condition, t=0). Gap opening requires t_gap ~ 100-200 orbital periods at the planet semi-major axis (a=20 au -> ~9000-18000 yr). The analysis therefore cannot test the Kanagawa prediction; Sigma_gap/Sigma_0 = 1.0 is trivially the initial condition.
discrepancies.resolution: Run gap_1Mjup.par to completion (1000 orbits, Ntot=20000). The .par file is already fully configured.

discrepancies.description: The analysis-agent read from /Users/giovanni/Codes/fargo3d/data/runs/fargo_skill_test instead of data/runs/gap_1Mjup/. The fargo_skill_test run appears to be a quick skill-validation run at a=1 au (gap_location_au=0.408 ~ r=0.4 in the inner domain), not the science run at a=20 au.
discrepancies.resolution: Rerun analysis-agent pointing to data/runs/gap_1Mjup/ once the gap_1Mjup simulation completes.

discrepancies.description: The stated a_max(10 au) = 1.95e-4 cm (fragmentation-limited) from the DustPy skill does not match the value extracted directly from data/dust/iceline_test/data0009.hdf5 using the maximum-populated-bin definition (24.3 cm at r~10 au, same as outer disc). The DustPy run grid spans only r=1.1-89.7 au with Nr=20 and t_end=1000 yr (too short for full grain growth equilibrium in the outer disc). The stated value likely uses a surface-density-weighted mean grain size or comes from a different run.
discrepancies.resolution: Re-run DustPy with t_end=1e6 yr and Nr>=100 for a settled grain size profile. Clarify whether a_max refers to the maximum populated bin or the mean/median grain size.

follow_up_directions.title: Run gap_1Mjup.par to 1000 orbits and measure Sigma_gap/Sigma_0
follow_up_directions.description: Launch the existing gap_1Mjup FARGO3D setup (already configured for Ntot=20000, Ninterm=200, 1000 orbits at a=20 au) on a compute node. Extract the azimuthally-averaged gas surface density at t=500 and t=1000 orbits and compute Sigma_gap/Sigma_0. Compare against the Kanagawa prediction of 8.5e-3 (+/-30%). This is the primary test of Hypothesis H3.
follow_up_directions.expected_outcome: Sigma_gap/Sigma_0 should converge to 0.007-0.011 (within the Kanagawa 30% systematic uncertainty band) by t~200 orbits and remain stable thereafter.
follow_up_directions.estimated_cost: ~5000 core-hours on LRZ (256x512 grid, 20000 steps); wall-time ~8 h on 8 cores
follow_up_directions.quantitative_test: Pass if |Sigma_gap_sim / Sigma_gap_Kanagawa - 1| < 0.3; fail (potential RWI or 3D effect) if ratio < 0.5 or > 2.0

follow_up_directions.title: M_p scan: 6-point grid from 0.1 to 3 M_Jup, verify K power-law scaling
follow_up_directions.description: Run FARGO3D for M_p in [0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 3.0] M_Jup (all other parameters fixed: alpha=1e-3, h/r=0.05, a=20 au, 512x1024 grid, 1000 orbits each). Measure Sigma_gap/Sigma_0 at t=500 orbits for each run. Fit the power law Sigma_gap/Sigma_0 = 1/(1 + 0.04*K) and verify the exponent on q (should be q^2 -> slope = -2 in log-log K vs Sigma_gap).
follow_up_directions.expected_outcome: For M_p < M_gap_visc = 0.093 M_Jup (K < 25), Sigma_gap/Sigma_0 > 0.5 (partial gap). For M_p > 0.4 M_Jup (K > 300), Sigma_gap/Sigma_0 < 0.1 (deep gap). At 1 M_Jup the prediction is 8.5e-3. Deviation at M_p > 2 M_Jup (K > 11000) would indicate the formula saturates or the Rossby Wave Instability fragments the gap edge.
follow_up_directions.quantitative_test: Slope of log(1/Sigma_gap - 1) vs log(q) should be 2.00 +/- 0.15 if Kanagawa power law holds

follow_up_directions.title: RADMC-3D synthetic ALMA image: predicted 1.25 mm gap signature
follow_up_directions.description: Use the converged FARGO3D gas Sigma(r) from F1 as input to a DustPy run with the gap modulation applied (multiply gas Sigma by the measured Sigma_gap/Sigma_0 profile in the gap region). Compute dust Sigma(r, a) with DustPy for t=1 Myr. Pass the dust density cube to RADMC-3D (radmc3d image lambda=1250 incl=30 posang=0) and convolve with ALMA beam FWHM=35 mas at d=140 pc (Taurus-like distance). Compare predicted gap contrast and width against the DSHARP survey (Andrews+2018 2018ApJ...869L..41A [VERIFY], Zhang+2018 2018ApJ...869L..47Z [VERIFY]).
follow_up_directions.expected_outcome: For K=2916 the gas gap is 118x depleted; the mm-grain dust gap is expected to be deeper (factor ~3-10 additional depletion) due to Stokes-number-dependent trapping outside the gap. Predicted ALMA flux contrast (gap/ring) should be < 0.05 at 1.25 mm.
follow_up_directions.quantitative_test: Synthetic ALMA gap depth (1 - I_gap/I_ring) should exceed 0.95 for a 1 M_Jup planet at 20 au; if contrast < 0.7, dust opacity or inclination effects need to be revisited

warnings: Kanagawa formula calibrated on 2D isothermal simulations; 3D and non-isothermal corrections are ~20-30%; K=2916 is at the edge of the calibration range

At K=2916 the Rossby Wave Instability (RWI) may be triggered at the steep gap edges (Lovelace+1999 [2016PASJ...68...43K ref]); this would produce vortices and invalidate the axisymmetric Kanagawa gap profile

DustPy a_max(10 au) = 1.95e-4 cm (stated) does not match direct extraction from data0009.hdf5 (24.3 cm); this discrepancy must be resolved before using the dust results — likely a run-config or metric-definition mismatch
DustPy run used t_end=1000 yr; grain growth equilibrium at r > 30 au requires t > 1 Myr; stated outer-disc a_max may not be converged
The fargo_skill_test run read by the analysis-agent has gap_location_au=0.408, inconsistent with the intended planet location of 20 au; this run should not be used as a science baseline
All DSHARP bibcodes except 2016PASJ...68...43K are marked [VERIFY IN ADS]; do not cite without cross-checking against NASA ADS
